newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 30.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government is considering an emergency package of new federal taxes which will need to go ahead if the High Court strikes down A$5 billion worth of State taxes, including business franchise fees, and tobacco, alcohol and petrol taxes, next wee. The Commonwealth will hand back any revenue from the taxes to the States. Page 1.

The release yesterday of Australian Bureau of Statistics trade figures showing a record trade surplus for Australia of A$1.96 billion in June, look like leading Australia to recording its lowest quarterly account deficit in ten years. Yesterday's figures follow a revised surplus of A$787 million for May. Page 3.

Federal Cabinet's next meeting, which will concentrate wholly on Australia's unemployment problem, will consider job creation schemes, such as "life-long learning accounts", sending public sector "back office" operations out to country areas, and improving labour market mobility. Page 3.

A Newspoll survey funded by the New South Wales Roads and Traffic Authority has found Australians are happy to work from home using computers and telephones. According to the survey, 10 per cent of workers in the State already work from home, and experts believe this figure could more than double. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Trade figures released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the sell-off of Australia's gold reserves by the Reserve Bank last month assisted in lifting the nation's trade surplus to a record A$2.8 billion for the year just ended. The figures, which come after four years of deficits, were also assisted by strong exports of wheat, oil, gas and cars. Page 1.

A meeting of State and Federal health and police ministers tomorrow will hear a presentation by the Federal Government of an overhaul of Australia's anti-drug effort, with Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge expected to support the ACT's controversial heroin trial and Victoria's alternative heroin-addiction treatment. There will also be increased pressure for a national drugs summit. Page 1.

A United Nations-sponsored conference in Geneva today will be attended by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission commissioner on native title Geoff Clark, who will attack the Federal Government's race policies, and Aboriginal Affairs Minister Jon Herron, who is expected to tell the conference the Government is fighting poverty. Page 1.

The Office of the New South Wales Legal Services Commissioner yesterday warned it will crack down on lawyers who try to intimidate dissatisfied clients to stop them complaining to a legal watchdog, following several cases of lawyers threatening to sue clients for defamation. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia posted a record trade surplus yesterday, moving almost A$2 billion into the black in June thanks to the Reserve Bank's gold sell-off. While the gold sale boosted what the Federal Government described as "fantastic figures", Australian still recorded a A$153 million trade surplus without the one-off boost. Page 1.

The New South Wales Johnes Disease Steering Committee has directed the slaughter of at least 320,000 sheep in 183 flocks across the State as part of a bid to eradicate Orvine Johnes Disease (OJD). The Committee has suggested two to three more infections exist for every known infection, and this could lift the number of sheep slaughtered to one million. Page 1.

New research conducted by the University of Melbourne has found children who have poor literacy skills are being wrongly labelled as inattentive and referred for counselling and medical attention. The research, by educational psychologist Ken Rowe, suggests improved teaching skills will solve classroom behaviour problems. Page 1.

Care agency Barnardos head Louise Voigt yesterday claimed that millions of dollars had been squandered by the New South Wales Department of Community Services, which had done little to improve the State's care system. Voigt said State wards face deteriorating conditions as money is spent on unproductive internal reviews. Page 3.
THE AGE

Initial treatment has failed to killed off Prime Minister John Howard's severe bout of pneumonia, and he has been urged by his family, advisers and doctors not to return to work until completely fit so as not to cause a relapse. Trade Minister Tim Fische and Treasurer Peter Costello will share leadership responsibilities until Howard recovers. Page 1.

A secret Federal Government study to be considered tomorrow by the ministerial drug council has found the number of people dying from heroin overdoses each year has risen by 700 per cent in the 15 years to 1995, and the figure may not have peaked. The reort claims users will be at the greatest risk 10 years from now. Page 1.

Talks between the Victorian Government and transport unions are stalled, which could mean a repeat of yesterday's 24-hour public transport strike. The strike, which disrupted Melbourne's roads and workplaces, is estimated to have cost the economy about A20 million. Page 1

The generation of baby boomers are showing their political influence as pharmaceutical companies and the Federal Government are ready to assist in the generally over-50s problem of impotence. Drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn has introduced Prostaglandin B, which is said to be a wonder drug for men suffering the problem. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
